reception: Citing works engage Vemal almost entirely from a distance: none extends the method or deploys the learned policy, and the record is peripheral throughout. The paper appears as an example — one of the demonstrations that learned policies can stand in for hand-written compiler heuristics — in a survey of machine learning for computer architecture and systems, in a taxonomy of ML for systems problems, and in the related-work sections of learned-optimization efforts such as ProGraML, RL4ReAl, and work on vectorization heuristics in dynamic compilers. The literature records it as a data point in a trend rather than a foundation.
